newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SMALL AT CENTRE OF TUG-OF-WAR.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SMALL AT CENTRE OF TUG-OF-WAR.

text.p: South African winger James Small is at the centre of a provincial tug-of-war that could see him become the second player in South African rugby history to move following the payment of a transfer fee.
Western Province have approached his present province Natal with a view to signing the 28-year-old winger, who has scored 14 tries in 36 tests. Natal were due to discuss the approach on Wednesday.

If Natal agree to the move Western Province will have to pay a 250,000 rands ($54,500) fee for the player, the maximum permitted under new regulations recently agreed by the South African Rugby Football Union.
Springbok flanker Andre Venter was the first player to be the subject of a fee when Transvaal paid Free State 250,000 rands for him earlier this year.
"It's got nothing to do with Natal or Durban -- I love both -- but Cape Town is my home,'' Small said.
"I've been with Natal for four years but I probably only spend four months of the year there. Travelling is taking its toll and I want to settle down and have a family. I want to move to Cape Town."
